laws.name: Amphibolite
laws.note: Dislocation: Hacker & Christie (1990), p. 139: A = (1.1 ± 0.3)e-4 MPa^-3.7 s^-1, n = 3.7, Q = 244 kJ/mol; synthetic amphibolite, 650-850 °C, 1 GPa confining pressure, differential stress. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.12 ± 0.22 (N = 14, Table 3, faulted runs excluded as in the paper), and the Fig. 16 lines within 0.15 dex. The 950 °C runs follow a separate law (p. 140) not covered here.

laws.name: Anhydrite
laws.note: Dislocation: Dorner et al. (2014), Eq. 4 (p. 810), indentation creep converted to uniaxial reference stress and strain rate (Eqs. 1-2; c1 = 0.296, c2 = 0.755), 708-920 °C, 1 atm: A = 4.8e-19 Pa^-3.9 s^-1, n = 3.9, Q = 338 kJ/mol (the 388 kJ/mol in the Conclusions is a typo). Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.01 ± 0.13 (N = 17, Table 1), and the Fig. 8 flow-law curves within about 0.1 dex.

laws.name: Antigorite
laws.note: Peierls: Burdette & Hirth (2022), Eq. 1 and Table 2: ε̇ = A (σ/μ)² exp(-(ΔF/RT)(1-(σ/τ0)^p)^q), ln A = -0.624 (A in s^-1), μ = 35 GPa, ΔF = 86.3 kJ/mol, τ0 = 2.42 GPa, p = 1 (imposed), q = 1.18; σ is differential stress. Intact antigorite cores, 1 GPa, 75-550 °C, Griggs apparatus. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.01 ± 0.10 (N = 57, digitized from Fig. 5b; tabulated data are in Supporting Information S1), and the Sect. 4.5 viscosities at 50 MPa shear stress within 0.1 dex.

laws.name: Blueschist
laws.note: Diffusion: Tokle et al. (2023), Eq. 5 (p. 10) and p. 12: A = 2.43e11 MPa^-2 μm s^-1 for σ_eqv = 2τ and ε̇_eqv = γ̇/√3, stored as SimpleShear with A = √3 × 2.43e11; n = 2, p = -1 with d = arithmetic-mean microboudin neck length, Q = 384 kJ/mol. Na-amphibole blueschist, ~1 GPa, 650-700 °C, Griggs general shear. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit 0.02 ± 0.07 (N = 20, Table 1), and the Fig. 3b lines within 0.03 dex.

laws.name: Calcite (coarse-grained, dislocation, X_MgCO3 = 0.001)
laws.note: Dislocation: Gilgannon & Herwegh (2025, preprint), Eq. 7 and Table 5 (pp. 17-18): A = 2.16e-8 s^-1 × X_MgCO3^-0.6 with σ_ref = 1 MPa, n = 7; X_MgCO3 = 0.001 (the paper's pure-calcite limit, p. 21) is folded into A. Q = 200 kJ/mol is assumed. Stress is equivalent stress. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit +0.12 ± 0.61 (N = 18, digitized from Fig. 4b), and the Fig. 10c-d curves within 0.05 dex in stress. The Fig. 6d curves lie about 1 dex slower than Table 5 and are inconsistent with Figs. 4b and 10.

laws.name: Calcite (fine-grained, diffusion, X_MgCO3 = 0.001)
laws.note: Diffusion: Gilgannon & Herwegh (2025, preprint), Eq. 5 and Table 5 (pp. 17-18): A = 3.40e7 s^-1 × X_MgCO3^0.8 with σ_ref = 1 MPa, d_ref = 1 μm; X_MgCO3 = 0.001 (the paper's pure-calcite limit, p. 21) is folded into A. This extrapolates below the fine-grained calibration range X_MgCO3 = 0.07-0.17. Q = 200 kJ/mol is assumed, not fitted. Stress is equivalent stress (torsion data converted with σ = √3 τ). Reproduces the Fig. 6a lines at σ = 1 MPa within 0.01 dex; with calcite_fine_dislocation_Gilgannon_2025 at each sample's X_MgCO3, log10 misfit -0.20 ± 0.17 (N = 72, digitized from Fig. 6a).

laws.name: Calcite (fine-grained, dislocation, X_MgCO3 = 0.001)
laws.note: Diffusion: Gilgannon & Herwegh (2025, preprint), Eq. 6 and Table 5 (pp. 17-18): A = 4.00e-8 s^-1 × X_MgCO3^-2.7 with σ_ref = 1 MPa, d_ref = 1 μm, n = 7, d^-3; X_MgCO3 = 0.001 (the paper's pure-calcite limit, p. 21) is folded into A. This extrapolates below the calibration range X_MgCO3 = 0.07-0.17. Q = 200 kJ/mol is assumed. Stress is equivalent stress. With calcite_diffusion_Gilgannon_2025 at each sample's X_MgCO3, reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.20 ± 0.17 (N = 72, digitized from Fig. 6a). The n = 7 guide line of Fig. 4a implies A ≈ 9.1e-8 instead (0.36 dex faster); the Table 5 value is kept.

laws.name: CO2 ice
laws.note: Dislocation: Durham et al. (1999), Eq. 1 and text (p. 3494): A = 10^3.86 MPa^-5.6 s^-1, n = 5.6, Q = 33 kJ/mol; polycrystalline CO2 ice, 150-190 K, 5-40 MPa confining pressure (no first-order pressure effect), differential stress. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.10 ± 0.40 (N = 26, Table 1; the paper notes six points outside their error bars).

laws.name: Columbia weak diabase
laws.note: Dislocation: Mackwell et al. (1998), flow law p. 980 and Table 2 (p. 978): A = 190 ± 110 MPa^-4.7 s^-1, n = 4.7, E = 485 kJ/mol; dry Columbia diabase, 940-1040 °C, 400-450 MPa confining pressure, gas-medium apparatus, differential stress. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit 0.03 ± 0.25 (N = 65, Table 2).

laws.name: Diabase
laws.note: Dislocation: Maryland diabase. Caristan (1982), p. 6789 (text beside Fig. 10): ε̇ = A σ^n exp(-Q/RT) with A = 6.12e-2 MPa^-n (s^-1), n = 3.05, Q = 276 kJ/mol, cited from Caristan's thesis; experiments in an argon gas-medium apparatus at 1000 °C, as-received samples, differential stress. Matches Carter & Tsenn (1987), Table 4 (n = 3.05, log A = -1.2 MPa^-n/s, Q = 276 kJ/mol, triaxial compression, 900-1000 °C; listed as dry), and Bremond d'Ars et al. (1999). Primary data: Caristan (1982), Table 1 creep points at 1000 °C (log10 misfit -0.37, N = 6); the temperature dependence comes from Caristan (1980, thesis), not available.

laws.name: Diabase, as-received (wet)

laws.name: Dry Anorthite
laws.note: Dislocation: Rybacki & Dresen (2000), Table 2, 'Dislocation creep, dry': log A = 12.7 MPa^-n/s, n = 3, Q = 648. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.06 ± 0.09 (N = 20, Table 1). Diffusion: Rybacki & Dresen (2000), Table 2, 'Diffusion creep, dry': log A = 12.1 MPa^-n μm^m/s, Q = 467 kJ/mol, m = 3. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.03 ± 0.09 (N = 19, Table 1).

laws.name: Dry Anorthite
laws.note: Dislocation: Rybacki et al. (2006), Table 5, 'Dislocation creep, dry': log A = 12.7 MPa^-n/s, n = 3, Q = 641, V = 24 cm^3/mol. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.06 ± 0.09 (N = 20; primary data: Rybacki & Dresen 2000, Table 1, which Table 5 refits). Diffusion: Rybacki et al. (2006), Table 5, 'Diffusion creep, dry': log A = 12.1 MPa^-n μm^m/s, Q = 460 kJ/mol, V = 24 cm^3/mol, m = 3. Table 5 refits the Rybacki & Dresen (2000) data (primary data: Rybacki & Dresen 2000, Table 1): log10 misfit -0.04 ± 0.09 (N = 19). Vs the 2006 paper's own dry runs it is about 4× too fast (+0.64 ± 0.26, N = 113); the paper's direct fit to those is log A = 12.4, Q = 482, V = 32.4 cm^3/mol.

laws.name: Dry Clinopyroxene
laws.note: Dislocation: Bystricky & Mackwell (2001), eq. (2), natural Sleaford Bay clinopyroxenite: ε̇ = 10^9.8 σ^4.7 exp(-760 kJ/mol / RT), ε̇ in s^-1, σ = σ1 - σ3 in MPa. Same values in Bürgmann & Dresen (2008), Suppl. Table 1. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.01 ± 0.09 (N = 28, Table 2, natural samples). Diffusion: Bystricky & Mackwell (2001), eq. (5), diffusion term (dry hot-pressed clinopyroxenite, Ni/NiO buffer): ε̇ = 10^15.1 σ d^-3 exp(-560 kJ/mol / RT), ε̇ in s^-1, σ = σ1 - σ3 in MPa; d in μm (unit not printed, implied by the 8 μm normalisation and the strain rates). Same values in Bürgmann & Dresen (2008), Suppl. Table 1. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit 0.00 ± 0.15 (N = 20, Fig. 5 curves, d = 8 μm).

laws.name: Dry Clinopyroxene
laws.note: Diffusion: Hier-Majumder et al. (2005), eq. (3) and Table 3, row 'Anhydrous': ε̇ = ε̇o (σ/G)^n (d/do)^p exp(-Q/RT) with ε̇o = 10^25.3 s^-1, n = 1, p = -3, Q = 760 kJ/mol, G = 64.9 GPa, do = 10 μm, σ differential stress. In MPa and μm: A = ε̇o do^3 / G = 10^25.3 × 10^3 / 64.9e3 = 3.07e23 MPa^-1 μm^3/s (equal to Bürgmann & Dresen 2008, 10^25.3/64.9; the former 10^25.3/64.9e3 lacked the do^3 factor). Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit +0.03 ± 0.10 (N = 36, Table 2a).

laws.name: Dry Diopside
laws.note: Dislocation: Dimanov & Dresen (2005), Table 3b, row DiD: A = 3.01e-28 Pa^-n/s, n = 5.47, Q = 691. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.08 ± 0.07 (N = 14, Table 1, dislocation-dominated). Diffusion: Dimanov & Dresen (2005), Table 3b, row Di35D (n = 1, Q = 528); A = 10^14 from Bürgmann & Dresen (2008), Suppl. Table 1, since the paper folds d^m into A (m = 3 assumed). A implies an effective grain size of about 13-15 μm, which the paper does not state (it gives only particle size classes).

laws.name: Dry Dunite
laws.note: Dislocation: Chopra & Paterson (1984), p. 7865 and Table 3, row 'Both dunites, dry': ε̇ = A σ^n exp(-Q/RT) with A = 10^(4.46 ± 0.18) s^-1 MPa^-n, n = 3.60 ± 0.22, Q = 535 ± 33 kJ/mol (± 2 standard deviations), σ = differential stress; one multilinear regression of the Table 2 data on Anita Bay (100 μm) and Åheim (900 μm) dunite, predried for > 60 h at 1200 °C, gas-medium apparatus, 300 MPa confining pressure, 1200-1400 °C, 1e-4 to 1e-6 s^-1. No separate law per rock and no activation volume (V = 0). Same values in Kirby & Kronenberg (1987), Table 1. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.02 ± 0.17 (N = 22, Table 2 predried runs without the two upper-limit rates of run 4580; Anita Bay +0.03 ± 0.20, N = 11; Åheim -0.07 ± 0.11, N = 11).

laws.name: Dry Dunite (fO2-dependent)
laws.note: Dislocation: Keefner et al. (2011), Table 3 (p. 7): A = 10^2.6 MPa^-3.6 Pa^-0.2 s^-1 (stored as 10^3.8 MPa^-3.8 s^-1), n = 3.6 (3.59), r = 0.2 with f = fO2 in Pa (not fH2O), E = 449 kJ/mol; Åheim dunite, d ≈ 0.9 mm, gas-medium apparatus, 300 MPa, 1150-1277 °C, IW to NNO buffers, differential stress. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit 0.02 ± 0.13 (N = 55, Table 2, 1250 °C runs where fO2 is given), and the Fig. 6a,c lines within 0.1 dex.

laws.name: Dry Eclogite
laws.note: Dislocation: Zhang & Green (2007), Table 2 and text p. 104: A = 10^3.3 MPa^-3.5 s^-1, n = 3.5, E = 403 kJ/mol, V = 27.2 cm³/mol (ΔH = 485 kJ/mol at 3 GPa); differential stress, Griggs axial compression; 50 Grt, 40 Omp, 10 Qz, 2.5-3.5 GPa, 1027-1327 °C. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.10 ± 0.21 (N = 16, Table 2), and the Fig. 4a-c fitted lines within 0.25 dex.

laws.name: Dry Olivine
laws.note: Peierls: Demouchy et al. (2013), eq. (4) and Table 2 'Model 3': A = 1e6 1/s, Q = 450 kJ/mol, σP = 15 GPa, p = 1/2, q = 2; σ is the differential stress. Reproduces the paper's Fig. 10b 'model 3' curve within 10 MPa (N = 13, 820-1540 K).

laws.name: Dry Olivine
laws.note: Diffusion: Faul & Jackson (2007), eq. (2) and paragraph [32]: A = 2e10 MPa^-n μm^p/s, E = 484 kJ/mol, n = 1.37, p = 3; dry, melt-free sol-gel olivine, V not determined. Formerly wet_olivine_Faul_2006. The 'mm' printed in the PDF for A and the grain size is a misprint for μm. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit +0.02 ± 0.09 (N = 77, Table 1, melt-free runs).

laws.name: Dry Olivine
laws.note: Dislocation: Gerya (2010), Exercise 6.1: A = 2.5e-17 Pa^-n/s, n = 3.5, Ea = 532 kJ/mol, Va = 0, 'representative for dry olivine', axial compression (2010 edition checked); the same law is in Gerya (2010), Table 17.1 (2.5e4 MPa^-n/s, 3.5, 532), 'from compilation by Ranalli, 1995'. Ranalli (1995) was not checked. The values are consistent with the arithmetic mean of the three dry-olivine rows of Kirby & Kronenberg (1987), Table 1: Karato et al. 1982 (log A = 3.9 MPa^-n/s, n = 3.5, H = 528 kJ/mol), Kirby 1983 (4.8, 3.5, 533) and Chopra & Paterson 1984 (4.46, 3.6, 535) give log A = 4.39 (2.44e4; Ueda et al. 2008, Table 1, print 10^4.4), n = 3.53 and H = 532.0. Primary data: Chopra & Paterson (1984), Table 2 (predried Anita Bay and Åheim dunite, 1200-1400 °C, 300 MPa): log10 misfit -0.23 ± 0.17 (N = 22, 1.7× too slow), while their own law (dry_dunite_Chopra_1984) fits at -0.02 ± 0.17. The Karato et al. (1982) and Kirby (1983) inputs were not checked against data. Valid for olivine under upper mantle conditions. Ranalli & Murphy (1987) is not the source: its only olivine law is n = 3, Q = 540 kJ/mol (A = 4.0e15 GPa^-n s^-1), a theoretical best fit from Ranalli (1982).

laws.name: Dry Olivine
laws.note: Peierls: Goetze & Evans (1979), eq. (1a), p. 469: ε̇ = 5.7e11 exp(-Q/RT (1 - σ/σP)^2), Q = 128 kcal/mol, σP = 8.5 GPa, σ = σ1 - σ3 (p = 1, q = 2). Reproduces the Goetze curve of Mei et al. (2010), Fig. 6, within 10 MPa (N = 8, 650-1350 K) and the paper's Fig. 4 Peierls curve up to about 1200 °C. Primary data: Evans & Goetze (1979), microindentation hardness of olivine single crystals (not checked here).

laws.name: Dry Olivine
laws.note: Dislocation: NOTE: the printed law is 2.5× too slow vs the paper's own data: -0.40 log10 units vs the Fig. 2a dislocation-creep fit line, -0.30 ± 0.19 vs the primary data, Mei & Kohlstedt (2000b), Table 1, dry runs (N = 12, diffusion removed) and -0.34/-0.48 vs Karato & Jung (2003), Table 1; a data-consistent version is dry_olivine_Hirth_2003_refit. Hirth & Kohlstedt (2003), Table 1, row 'dry dislocation': A = 1.1e5 MPa^-n/s, n = 3.5, E = 530; V = 14 cm^3/mol from Table 2 (range 13.4-27). Diffusion: Hirth & Kohlstedt (2003), Table 1, row 'dry diffusion': A = 1.5e9 MPa^-1 μm^3/s, E = 375, V = 2-10 (upper end used). Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit +0.16 ± 0.21 (N = 8; primary data: Mei & Kohlstedt 2000b, Table 1, dry runs at σ ≤ 60 MPa).

laws.name: Dry Olivine
laws.note: Peierls: Idrissi et al. (2016), eq. (1) and Table 1: A = 1e6 1/s, Q = 566 kJ/mol, σ0 = 3.8 GPa, p = 0.5, q = 2 (uniaxial stress). Renamed from dry_olivine_Idrissei_2016. Reproduces the paper's Fig. 1 law at 1e-5 s^-1 within 10 MPa (N = 10, 208-1103 K).

laws.name: Dry Olivine
laws.note: Dislocation: Karato & Jung (2003), Table 3 (open system) and abstract: A_d = 10^6.1 s^-1 MPa^-n, n = 3.0, r = 0, E*_d = 510 kJ/mol (taken there from Mei & Kohlstedt 2000), V*_d = 14 cm^3/mol. σ is differential stress (dislocation-density piezometer; Griggs simple-shear runs converted assuming isotropic plasticity). Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.07 ± 0.24 (N = 5, Table 1 dry).

laws.name: Dry Olivine
laws.note: Peierls: Mei et al. (2010), eq. (3) and paragraph [23]: A_P = 1.4e-7 MPa^-2/s, σP = 5.9 GPa, E_k(0) = 320 kJ/mol, p = 1/2, q = 1 (axial strain rate, differential stress). Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.09 ± 0.18 (N = 11, Table 1).

laws.name: Dry Olivine (refit to data)
laws.note: Dislocation: NOTE: refit of dry_olivine_Hirth_2003 with A = 2.8e5 MPa^-n/s (= 1.1e5 × 10^0.40; not a printed value) so that the law reproduces the paper's own data. The printed A = 1.1e5 is -0.40 log10 units (2.5× too slow) vs the Hirth & Kohlstedt (2003) Fig. 2a dislocation-creep fit line (1250 °C, 300 MPa, σ = 89-250 MPa), -0.30 ± 0.19 vs the Mei & Kohlstedt (2000) dry data it was fitted to (N = 12, σ ≥ 150 MPa, diffusion creep removed) and -0.34/-0.48 vs the dry strengths of Karato & Jung (2003), Table 1. n = 3.5, E = 530 and V = 14 cm^3/mol as in dry_olivine_Hirth_2003, which holds the printed law (Table 1, row 'dry dislocation').

laws.name: Dry Quartzite
laws.note: Dislocation: NOTE: the law is -0.25 log10 units slower than the paper's Fig. 6, which implies A ≈ 9e-6. Brace & Kohlstedt (1980), Eq. 5 (p. 6250): A = 5e-6 MPa^-3 s^-1 (printed as 5 × 10^6, a misprint; 5e6 puts the 100 MPa depth at < 1 km), n = 3, Q = 190 kJ/mol; dry quartzite (data of Christie et al. 1979 and Heard & Carter 1968), σ1-σ3 < 1000 MPa, differential stress. Reproduces the paper's Fig. 6 100 MPa depths within 1 km; no data table.

laws.name: Dry Quartzite
laws.note: Dislocation: Jaoul et al. (1984), Table 1, row 1 (W-292, creep in CaCO3 assembly, vacuum heated at 685 °C for 4 days, 700-1050 °C, 1.5 GPa): A = 1.37 s^-1 kbar^-n, n = 2.8 ± 0.2, E = 44.0 ± 1.5 kcal/mol; σ = σ1 - σ3 in kbar (Griggs apparatus). A converted to 1.37 × 100^-2.8 = 3.44e-6 MPa^-n/s (previously 10^-5.415, of unknown origin). Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.10 ± 0.09 (N = 15, Fig. 5a).

(2021), flow law p. 5: A = 10^(-4.4 ± 0.2) MPa^-4.2 s^-1, n = 4.2, E = 260 kJ/mol; synthetic felsic granulite (65 Pl, 15 Qz, 9 Cpx, 6 Opx, 5 Amp), 827-927 °C, 1 GPa, Griggs apparatus; the paper says flow stress, taken as differential stress.

Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.04 ± 0.42 (N = 16 steady-state runs, Table 2), and the Fig. 6A isotherms within 0.05 in log σ.

laws.name: Felsic Granulite (refit to data)
laws.note: Dislocation: NOTE: refit of felsic_granulite_Wen_2021 with A = 10^-4.7 MPa^-4.2 s^-1 (best fit at the printed n = 4.2 and E = 260 kJ/mol: 10^-4.71; a free fit gives n = 4.14, E = 265). laws.name: Glaucophane
laws.note: Dislocation: Hufford et al. (2026), abstract (p. 1) and flow law (p. 11): A = 2.32e10 MPa^-3 s^-1 for σ_equiv = 2τ and ε̇_equiv = γ̇/√3, stored as SimpleShear with A = √3 × 2.32e10; n = 3 (imposed), Q = 450 kJ/mol. Glaucophane aggregates < 63 μm, 1 GPa, 600-700 °C, Griggs general shear. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit 0.00 ± 0.18 (N = 21 creep steps, Table 1), and the Fig. 8 lines within 0.02 dex.

laws.name: Glaucophane glide
laws.note: Peierls: Hufford et al. (2026), glide law (p. 11): ε̇ = A (σ/μ)² exp(-(H/RT)(1-σ/σP)^2), A = 10^38.0181 s^-1, μ = 60.6 GPa, σP = 22 GPa, H = 800 kJ/mol, p = 1, q = 2, for σ_equiv = 2τ and ε̇_equiv = γ̇/√3; stored as SimpleShear with A/μ² × √3. Glaucophane aggregates, 1 GPa, 600-700 °C, Griggs general shear. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit -0.02 ± 0.21 (N = 12 high-stress steps, Table 1).

laws.name: Granite
laws.note: Dislocation: Carter & Tsenn (1987), Table 4, 'Westerly granite, dry (Hansen & Carter, 1983)': log A = -5.7 MPa^-n/s, n = 3.3, Q = 186.5. Primary data: Hansen & Carter (1983), not available. For comparison only (not its source data): vs the dry Westerly granite of Carter et al. (1981), Fig. 8b (same laboratory, Pc = 1 GPa, 570-765 °C, 0.6-1.2 GPa) the law gives log10 misfit -0.21 ± 0.42 (N = 9; -0.74 at 570 °C, +0.19 at 765 °C), because Q = 186.5 kJ/mol exceeds the 106 kJ/mol of those data.

laws.name: Granite
laws.note: Dislocation: Tirel et al. (2008), Table 1, 'granite (anomaly)': A = 1.25e-9 MPa^-n/s, n = 3.2, Ea = 123 kJ/mol (cites Kirby & Kronenberg 1987). A hybrid of two links: A is the Kirby & Kronenberg (1987), Table 3, Westerly granite row of Carter et al. (1981) (tabulated 8.5 - 6 × 2.9 = -8.9, i.e. 1.26e-9 MPa^-n/s; the Table 3 header 'MPa^-n s^-1' is a misprint, log A in MPa^-n s^-1 = tabulated value - 6n, confirmed by Carter et al. 1981, eq. 12), while n = 3.2 and E = 123 are the means of the two K&K87 Westerly granite rows (Carter et al. 1981: 2.9, 106; Hansen & Carter 1982: 3.4, 139), as in Ranalli (1995) (Gerya 2010, Table 17.1: 1.8e-9, 3.2, 123). Carter et al. (1981), eq. (12): ε̇ = 1.4e-9 exp(-25.3 kcal/mol / RT) σ^2.9, σ (differential) in MPa. Primary data: Carter et al. (1981), Fig. 8b (dry Westerly granite, Pc = 1 GPa, 570-765 °C, σ = 0.6-1.2 GPa; 9 steady-state points read from the figure): log10 misfit -0.16 ± 0.13 (N = 9; -0.31 at 570 °C), where eq. (12) gives -0.04 ± 0.08. Because n and E differ from eq. (12), the law is 3× slower than eq. (12) at 600 °C and 100 MPa and 12× slower at 400 °C and 10 MPa. Identical to the granite row of Ranalli & Murphy (1987), Tectonophysics 132, Table 1 (A = 5.0 GPa^-n s^-1 = 1.26e-9 MPa^-n s^-1, n = 3.2, Q = 123 kJ/mol), which cites Kirby (1983).

laws.name: high pressure wet Quartzite
laws.note: Dislocation: Lusk et al. (2021), Table 2, row 'High pressure' (700-1600 MPa), and abstract: log A = -7.90 MPa^-(n+r)/s, n = 2.0, r = 0.49, Q = 77, V = 2.59 cm^3/mol (r and V from the 'representative reduced' fit). σ is von Mises equivalent stress = differential stress for axial tests. Pass f = fH2O in Pa. Reproduces the paper's data: log10 misfit +0.25 ± 0.46 (N = 158, Fig. 7a).

laws.name: High Stress Wet Dunite
laws.note: Dislocation: Chopra & Paterson (1981), Table IV, row 'Anita Bay dunite, constant ε̇ (σ > ~100 MPa)': log A = 3.98 ± 0.17 s^-1 MPa^-n, n = 3.35, Q = 444 kJ/mol; eq. (1) with differential stress, gas-medium apparatus, 300 MPa confining pressure, 'wet' (water from hydrous minerals). Matches Carter & Tsenn (1987), Table 4, and Kirby & Kronenberg (1987), Table 1.
